name: Do basement door framing requirements differ in the Denver metro area?

mainEntity.name: Do basement door framing requirements differ in the Denver metro area?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, homes frequently feature basement framing built over expansive bentonite clay soils. When framing interior doors in basements across areas like Centennial, Parker, or Aurora, floating wall techniques are typically required. Instead of fastening king and jack studs directly to a bottom plate anchored to the concrete, a gap is left with specialized floating hardware to accommodate soil heaving without buckling the door frame or upper floors. Always confirm local municipal building department requirements before modifying basement framing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, Denver-area basements often require floating wall framing to accommodate soil movement from expansive clay, preventing door frames from binding or buckling.
